title: Structured Failure architecture audit
summary: Evidence-separated comparative audit deciding whether ResultSafe Core should provide an optional or mandatory structured failure payload.

payload.question: Should ResultSafe Core define a portable structured Failure, and if so may it constrain the generic Result error parameter E?
methodology: Inspect public declarations and official project documentation rather than inferred implementation internals
Record directly supported observations separately from ResultSafe architectural interpretation
Score four explicit options with published criteria and weights totaling one hundred
Treat weighted scoring as decision support rather than mathematical proof of a normative choice

sources.observation: The standard enum carries an independently selected E value in its Err variant.
The public working draft defines error_type as E and stores a T or E object.
Failure is caller-selected but must conform to the Swift Error protocol.
The failure channel is fixed to Throwable rather than a separate generic error parameter.
Left conventionally represents failure while its A payload remains arbitrary.

sources.error_shape: Either a b = Left a | Right b
sources.observation: Left conventionally stores an error value without requiring a prescribed record.
The Error union case carries the independently selected TError value.
The public README documents an arbitrary E and mapErr changing that error type.
The API exposes an unconstrained generic E in the Left branch.

sources.error_shape: Cause<E> tree around expected E and runtime causes
sources.observation: Effect retains polymorphic E while Cause adds defects, interruption, and composition context.
Examples use both string literals and Error objects as independently selected E values.
The README declares arbitrary E and an operation that maps it to a different type.
The documented Result preserves an independently selected error reason E.
Left carries an arbitrary generic L conventionally used for failure.
The dynamic API stores arbitrary values in either variant without a fixed error record.
Failure has a separate covariant error type; exception specialization is only an alias.
The archived project README declares arbitrary values in generic Ok and Err variants.
Left is conventionally failure and preserves a caller-selected generic L.
The sealed generic API supports arbitrary typed logical errors in Left.
L is traditionally an error carrier but remains a caller-selected generic type.

sources.error_shape: Result<T> with one or more IError reasons
sources.observation: Failures use prescribed IError reason objects and may aggregate multiple errors.
The failure representation is a library-defined list of Error records with categories.

sources.error_shape: Result<T> with ResultStatus and status-specific data
sources.observation: Non-success is classified by a fixed status with optional status-specific payloads.
The general union has no designated error channel and preserves arbitrary alternatives.

criteria.measurement: Preserves existing generic Result and shipped error payload behavior
Provides stable language-neutral identity and transport semantics
Supports versioning and namespaced extension without central application-code ownership
Supports bounded validation, redaction rules, and diagnostic separation
Remains usable for small domain errors and explicit integrations
Projects consistently to TypeScript, Python, relational data, and SQLite
Aligns with directly observed practices without treating popularity as authority

costs: No shared codes, validation, redaction, or storage contract
Marker cannot establish portable fields or storage semantics

benefits: Adds portable structure without constraining E
costs: Requires explicit adoption and maintained projections
Breaking replacement of arbitrary domain E
Couples simple domain errors to platform structure

observations: Sixteen typed Result or Either APIs in the audited set directly preserve a caller-selected generic error type
Effect demonstrates that structured cause context can wrap and retain generic E instead of replacing it
Fixed structured systems disagree on required fields, multiplicity, categories, status, and exception semantics
Message is presentation data and is not a stable failure identity across localization or redaction
Absolute URI codes provide decentralized qualification without a hardcoded global application error registry
The existing ResultSafe FailureData name already denotes the generic ResultData failure branch and cannot be reused safely

conclusion.compatibility_rule: Result<T,E>, Err<E>, and transport FailureData<E> remain generic; structured Failure is an explicit payload selected by a caller or strict profile.

limitations: Public documentation can change after retrieval and this corpus does not mirror third-party pages
Weighted criteria encode ResultSafe priorities and are decision support rather than universal proof
README sources are identified separately from formal API and language documentation
